````markdown
---
sidebar_position: 10
description: HTML Content - how to find, install, and give feedback on early access builds.
slug: /early-access
---

# Early Access Builds

The publish and release cycle for custom visuals in Power BI can be quite long, and once a version is live in AppSource, getting a fix back through certification takes time. To catch issues before they reach everyone, HTML Content publishes early access builds through two channels - **Alpha** and **Beta** - ahead of each AppSource submission.

Anyone who wants to help test these builds is very welcome, and feedback is greatly appreciated.

## Is this for me? {#is-this-for-me}

A quick checklist of what you're signing up for:

- Early access builds are provided on the basis of giving feedback to the maintainer.
- They are **not supported for production use**.
- Formal documentation is not complete until a release is ready to publish, so some discovery may be required between builds. Major changes are documented under the 2.0 docs on this site, and the working [Change Log](/docs/next/change-log) is the best digest of what's going on.
- Early access builds are de-coupled from AppSource - they are not certified, and they do not self-update.
- Access to early builds is a two-way street - please [let us know](#providing-feedback) about anything you find, and you'll help everyone get a better release when it lands in AppSource.

## General information {#general-information}

### Two packages in every build {#two-packages}

Each channel build attaches two `.pbiviz` packages - one per [edition](/docs/next/visual-editions):

| Package | Edition | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `HTML-Content.<version>.pbiviz` | **HTML Content** | Full HTML rendering, including external content where your tenant allows it. |
| `HTML-Content-Secure.<version>.pbiviz` | **HTML Content Secure** | Sanitizes markup and blocks external communication, matching the behavior of the certified AppSource visual. |

:::note The Secure channel build is not certified
Channel builds are not tied to AppSource and carry none of the certification benefits of the published certified visual. The Secure package is provided so you can verify sanitization and external-communication blocking against your own content before the certified release catches up.
:::

### Side-by-side with your existing visuals {#side-by-side}

Channel builds use channel-specific visual IDs, so they can be side-loaded into a report alongside the AppSource visuals (or another channel's build) without replacing or interfering with them. They do not auto-update - you choose when to move to a newer drop by importing it. Importing a newer build of the same channel into a report replaces that channel's previous build.

### Identifying your build {#identifying-your-build}

The version shown inside Power BI reads `2.0.0.0` for **every** channel build - it does not identify the drop you're running. The package filename (for example, `HTML-Content.2.0.0.alpha-1.pbiviz`) is the real identifier, so keep track of which file you imported and quote the full filename when [providing feedback](#providing-feedback).

### Release notifications {#release-notifications}

If you don't mind the emails, you can subscribe to release notifications by watching the [GitHub repository](https://github.com/dm-p/powerbi-visuals-html-content) - [GitHub's notification docs](https://docs.github.com/en/account-and-profile/managing-subscriptions-and-notifications-on-github/setting-up-notifications/about-notifications) cover how to set this up.

## Providing feedback {#providing-feedback}

If something doesn't work as expected - or works particularly well - please [create an issue in the GitHub repository](https://github.com/dm-p/powerbi-visuals-html-content/issues). Detail makes all the difference:

- **The full package filename** (e.g. `HTML-Content.2.0.0.alpha-1.pbiviz`) - see [Identifying your build](#identifying-your-build).
- **Steps to reproduce** the issue.
- **Expected vs. actual behavior** - ideally including how it differs from the current AppSource release.
- **Screenshots or short videos** showing the problem.
- **Sample content, measures, or a workbook** (with public or anonymized data).

Please don't assume someone else has already reported an issue - if you see it, report it.

:::warning Test with copies
Test with **copies** of production reports, not the originals - that way you can easily revert without losing any work.
:::

## Alpha Channel {#alpha-channel}

The Alpha Channel carries the latest build for the current development effort - features may still be in flux between drops.

### Accessing the build {#alpha-accessing}

The Alpha Channel build is published to the [`alpha` release tag](https://github.com/dm-p/powerbi-visuals-html-content/releases/tag/alpha) in the visual's GitHub repository. It is always the latest alpha for the current development effort, and both `.pbiviz` packages are available in the list of assets at the bottom of the release page.

{/* TODO: screenshot of the alpha release page, highlighting the .pbiviz assets. */}

### Installing and identifying {#alpha-installing}

Install the build by [importing the downloaded `.pbiviz` into your report](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/developer/visuals/import-visual#import-a-visual-file-from-your-local-computer-into-power-bi). The visual appears in the **Visualizations** pane with its own channel-specific icon and is named to identify itself as an Alpha Channel build.

{/* TODO: screenshot of the alpha icon in the Visualizations pane and the landing page. */}

Remember: the in-product version reads `2.0.0.0` - [the package filename identifies your build](#identifying-your-build).

## Beta Channel {#beta-channel}

The Beta Channel carries release-candidate builds - feature-complete versions being validated ahead of an AppSource submission.

### Accessing the build {#beta-accessing}

The Beta Channel build is published to the [`beta` release tag](https://github.com/dm-p/powerbi-visuals-html-content/releases/tag/beta) in the visual's GitHub repository, with both `.pbiviz` packages in the release assets. A beta build is published when the current development effort reaches a release candidate - if the link shows no release, there isn't an active beta right now.

### Installing and identifying {#beta-installing}

Installation is the same as for the [Alpha Channel](#alpha-installing) - import the downloaded `.pbiviz` into your report. The Beta Channel build has its own icon and visual ID, so it can be installed alongside the AppSource visuals and any Alpha Channel build.

{/* TODO: screenshot of the beta icon in the Visualizations pane and the landing page. */}

Remember to quote the full package filename when [providing feedback](#providing-feedback).
````
